body:
### Summary

As `uv` uses hardlinks to install files in .venv modifying a file will modify it for all .venv using that package now and in the future.

This happens i.e. when manually doing fast test what upstream changes would do or even unindented if your IDE is not configured correctly and you perform a refactoring.

I didn't find anything besides cleaning the cache and reinstalling all polluted .venv that would fix / reinstall the modified file.

I am used to a similar behaviour in conda but it at least raised SafetyWarnings when this happened. `uv` just stays silent.

### Example

It would be great if uv could use the `.dist-info/RECORD` files to verify that the cache was unmodified. And if not print a warning, removes the package from cache and reinstall it.

> *The following ideas were suggested by Claude (AI). I only include them as options, ordered by preference.*
>
> 1. **`uv sync` (and `uv pip install/sync`) verifies installed packages against their `.dist-info/RECORD`.**
>    A cheap pre-check (size, mtime) could come first, the hash comparison second, or the full check could be opt-in (e.g. `uv sync --verify`).
>    On a mismatch: print a warning, remove the affected package from the cache, and reinstall it.
>    The cache entry must be invalidated too, because in hardlink mode it shares the modified file.
> 2. **A dedicated check command**, e.g. `uv cache check` / `uv cache verify` (cache entries against their `RECORD`) and/or a venv-side option such as `uv sync --check --verify`.
>    It should exit non-zero on a mismatch, with an optional `--fix`.
> 3. **Documentation only:** state in "Cache safety" and in the `link-mode` docs that, with hardlinks, editing a file in a venv also modifies the cache and all other venvs, and describe the recovery steps (`uv cache clean <pkg>`, then `uv sync --reinstall-package <pkg>` in each affected venv).
title: Modifying a file in a `.venv` silently corrupts the shared cache and all other venvs (hardlink mode), and uv has no way to detect or repair it
